tables.title: RDES3 normal descriptor (read format)
tables.text_helper: Table 836, "RDES3 normal descriptor (read format)", in section 76.10.4 (Receive descriptor) on page 4166. Columns: Bit, Name, Description. 6 data row(s).

rows:
Own bit
When this bit is set, it indicates that the DMA owns the descriptor. When this bit 
is reset, it indicates that the application owns the descriptor. The DMA clears this 
bit when either of the following conditions is true:
– The DMA completes the packet reception
– The buffers associated with the descriptor are full

Interrupt Enabled on Completion
When this bit is set, an interrupt is issued to the application when the DMA 
closes this descriptor.

Buffer 2 Address Valid
When this bit is set, it indicates to the DMA that the buffer 2 address specified in 
RDES2 is valid. The application must set this bit so that the DMA can use the 
address to which the Buffer 2 address in RDES0 is pointing, to write received 
packet data.

Buffer 1 Address Valid
When set, this indicates to the DMA that the buffer 1 address specified in RDES0 
is valid.
The application must set this value if the address to which Buffer 1 address 
points in RDES0, can be used by the DMA to write received packet data.
